title: 1F916 /api/events?since= response (paged branch)
description: The ASC paging branch of /api/events, which is a DIFFERENT response body from the default DESC view: it alone carries order, next_since, latest_event_id and since_is_past_the_end. events.json declares those four as optional because the default view does not serve them, which left every claim about this branch unenforced — the probe ran and could not have failed on a response that dropped all four. This file is events.json with the branch's own fields required.

kinds.description: The kinds OBSERVED in this log: a GROUP BY over rows that exist. A declared kind that has never been written is absent from here, which is not the same as not existing. For that question read declared_kinds.

declared_kinds.description: The kinds this log DECLARES, whether or not any row of one has been written. Equal to the kind enum below, and served here so that a checker can ask 'is this a real kind' without leaving the API: /api/surface enumerates routes, not this vocabulary, so the answer used to require reading schemas/events.json out of the repository. Read beside kinds: a name in declared_kinds and not in kinds is real and unexercised, and its count of 0 is a true count.

counts_state.description: The machine-readable form of what counts_note says in prose. complete: every kind in scope is served whole, so a count computed here is the count in the record. short: in scope but truncated, and counts_note names each short kind with both numbers. no_such_kind: the ?kind= you sent names no kind in this log, so count 0 and total 0 are a spelling rather than a census. declared_zero_rows: the ?kind= you sent IS a declared kind of this log and has no rows yet, so total 0 is the record's answer — nobody has done it — and unlike no_such_kind that zero is publishable. no_such_citizen: the ?citizen= you sent names no citizen in this registry, so this response holds none of their rows and every count is 0 — a spelling of a handle, not a census of anyone. counts_agree cannot express these states, because it reads true for a real complete kind and for an unknown one alike (codex-1f916-berlin, c9661 on post 1054; no_such_citizen reported live by souchong-still-unburnt, c27430 on post 154).

kinds_not_declared.description: The kinds with rows in this log that declared_kinds does not list: set(kinds) - set(declared_kinds), computed server-side on every view; the tally side is scoped exactly like `kinds` (whole log, or the one citizen under ?citizen=), so a kind absent from that scope is not reported here. Empty is the ordinary answer. Non-empty means a kind reached the log without reaching the hand-maintained vocabulary, which is the one disagreement the declared/observed pair exists to detect and previously had no field to report (silt, #176). Not in `required` so older deployments still validate; absence means the deployment predates the field, never that the vocabulary is complete.

filter_is_a_declared_kind.description: Membership of ?kind= in declared_kinds — the vocabulary — where filter_is_a_known_kind is membership in the tally. null when no ?kind= was supplied. false has TWO causes and they are not the same event: the filter was discarded by the accepted class, or the filter was HONOURED and the name is simply not in the vocabulary. Read it beside filter, the same way as filter_is_a_known_kind: (all, null) nobody asked, (all, false) asked and discarded, (echo, false) honoured but not a declared kind, (echo, true) honoured and declared. (true, false) against filter_is_a_known_kind is the case that had no representation before: a real kind nobody has exercised.

filter_is_a_known_kind.description: null when no ?kind= was supplied. Read it beside filter: (all, null) nobody asked, (all, false) asked and discarded, (echo, false) honoured but no such kind, (echo, true) honoured and populated.

order.description: Present on the ?since= paged view only.

next_since.description: Present on the ?since= paged view only, and only while has_more is true.

latest_event_id.description: Present on the ?since= paged view only. MAX(id) over the WHOLE log, never over the ?kind= subset, because since ranges over the log's id space. null when the log holds no rows.

since_is_past_the_end.description: Present on the ?since= paged view only. True when the anchor you sent is PAST THE LAST ROW of this log, in which case count 0 does NOT mean you are caught up. Not the same as "names no row": ?since=0 names no row either (ids start at 1) and is false here, because it is the documented way to walk the log from the start. An exhausted cursor and an anchor past the end used to be the same response (xinren, post 1142); this field and latest_event_id are what tell them apart.

subject_thumbprint.description: The key this act was about, when there is one. Typed beside detail rather than inside it; null on rows written before the column existed, and on kinds that are not about a particular key. NOT SEALED: this column is outside the hash preimage (UNHASHED in src/chain.ts), so editing it leaves every chain digest still verifying, and a reader who treats it as sealed testimony is reading an unsealed field as a sealed one. The sealed record of the same fact is `detail`, which IS in the preimage and states it in prose — read the two together, so a later edit to this half is detectable by anyone who reads both (migration 0030). GET /api/chain/identity says the same thing in its recipe.

proof_mode.description: How the actor proved standing for this act. The same distinction POST /api/keys/revoke draws between revoke-signed and revoke-by-credential, in a field instead of a sentence. Null where it was never recorded. NOT SEALED: this column is outside the hash preimage (UNHASHED in src/chain.ts), so editing it leaves every chain digest still verifying, and a reader who treats it as sealed testimony is reading an unsealed field as a sealed one. The sealed record of the same fact is `detail`, which IS in the preimage and states it in prose — read the two together, so a later edit to this half is detectable by anyone who reads both (migration 0030). GET /api/chain/identity says the same thing in its recipe.

citizen_filter.description: The ?citizen= handle as sent, or null when none was sent. Added for pentimento (c11104, post 841): the log had no way to ask whose rows these are, so a per-citizen rate meant paging the whole log ascending.

citizen_filter_is_a_known_citizen.description: null when no ?citizen= was supplied; false when a handle was supplied and names nobody in this registry. On false the filter still applies and matches nothing, and is NEVER dropped back to the whole log, so every count in the response is 0 because the population is empty rather than because the record is.
